newsitem.title: USA: House group subpoenas documents on Chinese embassy.
newsitem.headline: House group subpoenas documents on Chinese embassy.

text.p: The House committee investigating campaign funding abuses on Tuesday issued subpoenas to the White House and Justice Department to find out about any alleged Chinese government involvement in funnelling money for the 1996 presidential election.

Chairman Dan Burton, an Indiana Republican who heads the House Committee on Government Reform and Oversight, said the subpoenas are designed to find out if the Chinese Embassy in Washington played any role in fund raising.

It would be illegal for a foreign government to play any role in giving money to U.S. campaigns. The Chinese have denied as "groundless" reports they might have funnelled money into the campaign, though news reports said the FBI is looking into the matter.
"It is essential that we know what information was forwarded to the White House regarding the Justice Department's investigation into the activities of the Chinese Embassy, " said Burton.
"We must find out if this investigation was compromised in any way, and getting these documents and information will help us in making that determination."

Press reports have said the Justice Department obtained electronic intercepts "that point to a possible involvement by the Chinese Embassy in political fund raising during the last election," Burton said in a statement.

He said that it was a matter of public record that the White House had requested and received information from the Justice Department on the reported intercepts. Burton said that he wanted to find out what information the White House requested and what it received.
Separately Tuesday, minority Senate Democrats investigating campaign funds abuses sought subpoenas for 11 organisations that favoured Republicans, including the powerful Christian Coalition.

Sen. John Glenn, an Ohio Democrat who is the senior Democrat on the Senate committee headed by Tennessee Republican Sen. Fred Thompson investigating campaign funds, said the subpoenas he requested would bring some balance to the investigation.
So far the Republican-controlled committee over some Democratic objections has issued 54 subpoenas of people and documents mostly affecting Democratic fund raising.

A source close to Thompson said the Democratic requests for subpoenas would not be approved until the committee gets its funding. Democrats are protesting requests for $5.7 million that Thompson now wants to run the investigation.
Besides the Christian Coalition, Democrats want documents from foundations and non-profit organisations, including the National Right to Life anti-abortion group, that helped Republicans.
In a letter to Thompson that revealed the subpoenas, Glenn said he wanted the 11 Democratic-requested subpoenas "to restore some balance to the thrust of this investigation."
